_note: A quantifier is a claim about a SET, so the set is named and counted here the same way every numeral names its computation. This deck has one universal and it points at a population in the world rather than at objects the frame draws, which is the harder case. It is declared as such, with the exact claim sentence that bounds it, because a universal the record does not reach is the shape of overclaim this file exists to catch.

quantifiers.sentence: None of them asks the grid for anything.
quantifiers.set: the approximately 40 reciprocating gas engines Kodiak states it will supply to one West Texas data center, as drawn on frame 5 and as stated in c17
members: the approximately 40 reciprocating natural gas-fueled generation units of c17, which c16 states supply 76 megawatts of BEHIND-THE-METER, baseload power capacity to that one site
quantifiers.computed_by: behind_the_meter.units in out/2026-09-23/figures.json, parsed from c17's verbatim quote by compute.py, which is also the loop bound the frame draws its marks from
quantifiers.verified: the universal is carried entirely by the words BEHIND-THE-METER in c16's own quote. Power supplied behind a customer's meter does not enter the interconnection process, so no unit in this set is a request to connect. The sentence asserts nothing about any engine outside this one supply agreement, and the deck nowhere claims a statewide count of behind the meter units.
quantifiers.about: one stated supply agreement, not a population of gas engines in Texas. claims.json carries no statewide figure and the deck prints none.
quantifiers.what_it_does_not_claim: It does not claim these engines are unregulated, unpermitted or invisible to the state. The air permit question is a separate instrument and this deck refused to assert a mechanism there, because verification could not establish one.

quantifiers.sentence: The audit names one consequence and calls it denial of connection to the Texas grid.
quantifiers.set: the consequences stated in the August 3rd audit directive and restated in the September 21st release, read in full
members: denial of connection to the Texas grid for a project that fails to comply with the requirements set by the PUCT and ERCOT, c7
denial of interconnection for a project that fails to complete the audit process, c10
quantifiers.computed_by: the distinct consequences across every claim this run verified from the two audit documents, c5 through c10, which reduce to ONE: refusal of a grid connection. c7 and c10 are the same consequence stated twice in two documents, which is why the set has two members and a size of one
quantifiers.verified: read against the full text of both releases rather than against the quoted spans alone. Neither document names a fine, a revocation, a permit condition, an injunction or any consequence that reaches a project outside the interconnection process.
quantifiers.about: what the AUDIT directive names, not what the state can do to a data center in general. The water directive at c22 names a separate consequence under a separate instrument and this sentence makes no claim about it. The deck says so on its own closing surfaces rather than leaving the universal to stand wider than the document.
quantifiers.declared_voluntarily: quantifier_check did not flag this phrase. It is declared because it IS a universal about a set, and a universal nothing checks is one edit away from a universal nothing checks and is wrong.
quantifiers.restated: The declaration used to quote 'The only consequence the audit names is refusal of a connection to the Texas grid', which is what the frame said until round 5. The dek was rewritten to ATTRIBUTE rather than assert, because brand.yaml's voice.dont names calling ERCOT the Texas grid as the outsider tell, and this file kept the old string. A scorer found the declaration describing a frame that no longer exists. The universal itself did not move: it is still ONE consequence, still bounded by c7 and c10.

quantifiers.phrase: A machine standing on a pad is not asking for one
quantifiers.flagged_by: no gate, declared voluntarily after a round 4 scorer named it the deck's one undeclared generic
quantifiers.set: reciprocating gas engines supplying a site behind its meter, which is the class c16 and c17 describe and the class every machine drawn on this deck belongs to
quantifiers.note: The sentence is a generic about a CLASS and frame 2 cites c7 and c10, neither of which mentions behind the meter supply, so on that frame alone it reads as unsupported. What licenses it is deictic. The machine in the sentence is the machine drawn on the frame, the deck has already established at c16 and c17 what that machine is, and a set of engines supplying a site behind its meter is by definition not requesting an interconnection. It is not a claim that NO machine anywhere asks for a connection, which would be false and which no surface says.
quantifiers.sentence: A machine standing on a pad is not asking for one.
